publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: An original double side photolithography method on ultrathin polymer and a laser micromachining technique were used to fabricate different fishnet structures. We performed simulations and experiments by terahertz time domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS from 100GHz to 3THz) respectively. The effective parameters were extracted with a single shot approach.

articleTitle: Millimeter continuous wave imaging for non-destructive investigation of artistic materials
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A monochromatic millimeter wave system coupled with an infrared temperature sensor has been used to investigate pictorial artworks. The flexibility of the system makes it possible to rapidly reveal buried layer information such as a graphite handmade sketch covered by paintings.

articleTitle: Time-resolved THz-spectroscopy of InAs nano-wires
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We study the emission mechanisms of THz radiation from InAs nanowires (NWs) using femtosecond infrared (IR) pump beam and THz probe in a time-resolved reflection geometry setup at room temperature. We compare the spectra of InAs NWs with that of a p-InAs crystal which is standard THz emitter.

articleTitle: Physical optics characterization of a THz time domain system: UWB leaky lens antenna vs. Austin switch
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this work we show that a THz time domain system based on photoconductive antennas can be improved by over one order of magnitude by using the Ultra-wideband (UWB) leaky lens antenna. The system has been analyzed by implementing a physical optics method to characterize radiated fields by a silicon lens.

articleTitle: The THz spectra and analysis of Bi4Ge3O12 crystal
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: THz time domain spectra of Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>Ge<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> (BGO) crystal were measured. The refractive index and power absorption function and optical dielectric function were obtained. The time domain spectrum shows resonance characteristic. There was one strong absorption band in the range of 1.5-2.3 THz. And the refractive index exist abnormal dispersion in the range. The time domain spectra characteristic of photon-phonon interaction were presented and it show that the phonon polariton arises in BGO crystal.

articleTitle: Near-field spectra from broadband-infrared nanoscope
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We demonstrate 300 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> wide spectra in the 800-1400 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> range taken from single pixels of about 20 nm size. Technical issues of coupling a fiber-laser-powered coherent spectrometer with a standard near-field microscope will be discussed, together with results on the phonon-resonant response of numerous crystals. Quantitative amplitude and phase spectra will be compared with theory.

articleTitle: Electrical control of terahertz radiation through nanoresonators on VO2
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We demonstrate electrical control of terahertz radiation through nanoresonators on VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin film. By electrically induced insulator-to-metal phase transition, terahertz radiation can be switched-off. Transmission is decreased by one order of magnitude even when the film thickness is in nanoscale.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-based broadband terahertz modulators
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Broadband modulation of propagating terahertz waves at room temperature is demonstrated using subwavelength metallic slit arrays. Our designs enable the modulation of terahertz transmission by at least 55% at their modulation frequencies.

articleTitle: Composite left-right handed metamaterials at terahertz frequencies
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: High-transmissivity left/right-handed metamaterials were fabricated in a multilayered dielectric/hole metal array technology and experimentally assessed at sub-millimeter wave lengths. From the frequency dependence of the scattering parameters, we show the possibility to close the gap between the left- and right-handed dispersion branches.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of microwave electromagnetic shielding in carbon based epoxy nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on the comparative study of the effectiveness of electromagnetic shielding provided by different forms of nanocarbon dispersed in resin.

articleTitle: Terahertz radiation in an optical-field-induced ionization in air with a pulsed electrostatic field
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have demonstrated that the terahertz radiation can be generate by the burst current produced by a laser created ionization front, which is induced an optical-field-induced ionization in air with a pulsed electric field. The peak frequency of the radiation spectrum depends on the rise time of the OFI. The central frequencies of the radiation are observed to be 0.2 and 0.04 THz at the pulse durations of 50 and 300 fs (FWHM), respectively. The power of the linearly polarized THz radiation is linearly increased with the square of the electrostatic field strength applied to the capacitors.

articleTitle: Design of terahertz tunable filter using subwavelength metallic slit arrays
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A high quality tunable filter at terahertz frequencies has been designed using subwavelength metallic slit arrays. The bandpass center frequency is tunable over the range of 0.592 THz to 0.994 THz. Tunning is achieved by relative vertical movement of the subwavelength metallic slit layers.

articleTitle: Simulation of a four-stage depressed collector for a W-band Gyro-BWO
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: To improve the overall efficiency of the W-band gyrotron backward wave oscillator (gyro-BWO) currently being built in the University of Strathclyde, an energy recovery system using a four-stage depressed collector was simulated and designed. The spent beam information was exported from the simulation of the gyro-BWO using the 3D PIC code MAGIC. The geometry of the depressed collector was optimized using a genetic algorithm to achieve the optimum overall recovery efficiency for specific parameters of the spent beam. Secondary electron emissions were simulated to investigate the effects of the secondary electrons on the overall recovery efficiency and the backstreaming of the electrons from the collector region.

articleTitle: Anti-reflection coated lenses for THz applications
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have successfully coated with a repeatable and reliable technique large (up to 350 mm) polyethilene lenses for use at THz frequencies. The method described in detail is not dependant on the lens material. We also combined a canonical ray-tracing model with a local transmission line code to predict the spectral performance of coated lenses.

articleTitle: Precise analysis of Wood-Rayleigh anomalies in the terahertz transmission spectrum of a metallic hole array
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We derive a general expression for calculating the parameters of excitation of Wood and Rayleigh anomalies observed in the transmission spectrum of a hole array with square cells. An experimental validation of the model, using THz time-domain spectroscopy, is performed. The difference between s and p polarized transmitted signals allows us to clearly identify the signature of surface plasmon excitation.

articleTitle: Extreme-bandwidth THz pulses from laser-generated air plasmas
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present the generation of coherent terahertz radiation with a continuous spectrum covering the range up to above 100 THz, using an air-plasma with sub-20-fs two-color optical excitation, and demonstrate its potential for spectroscopic applications.

articleTitle: Real-time terahertz color scanner
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Real-time THz color scanner was proposed based on a combination of non-collinear electro-optical time-to-space conversion and line focusing of a THz beam. The proposed system has the potential to expand the application scope of THz spectral imaging based on its rapid image acquisition rate.

articleTitle: Ultrabroadband metamaterial with full transmission control
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We study log periodic nanoresonators on VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> thin film, amplifying available dynamic range for extinction and transmission. Over 1,000:1 extinction ratio for the nano-pattern is achieved when the film undergoes insulator-to-metal phase transition, compared with 10:1 ratio for the unpatterned cases.

articleTitle: Higher order conformation of Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate)s studied by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Terahertz absorption spectra of Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate)s were measured. The orientation of the transition dipole moment was investigated by the polarization spectra. The temperature dependence of the spectra reflects the change in the hydrogen bonding distance of the crystalline structure.

articleTitle: Generation of submillimeter radiation by strong plasma turbulence at electron beam — Plasma interaction
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Paper presents results of investigations of electromagnetic radiation emission in a submillimeter range at strong Langmuir turbulence pumped by a relativistic electron beam. Radiation at double plasma frequency is generated due to plasmon-plasmon merging. Results of radiation power measurements are compared with theoretical estimations.

articleTitle: Comparison of expressions for terahertz generation for bulk optical rectification away from normal incidence
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In a paper recently published by Hargreaves, Radhanpura and Lewis (HRL), the theory of bulk optical rectification under arbitrary excitation conditions for zinc blende crystals was developed. The results from HRL have since been compared to results in the literature for (100), (110), (111), and (112) crystal faces under normal incidence of the excitation beam and good agreement found. Under these conditions, many terms in the expressions become. The purpose of the current work is to compare the expressions at non-normal incidence to gain a more general comparison between the expressions in the literature.

articleTitle: Terahertz resonant artificial interface layers
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Planar metamaterials, so-called metasurfaces, can efficiently be described by a modified transfer matrix formalism, that takes into account anisotropic, conductive interfaces. This method is applied for evaluation of the transmission of THz pulses through different metasurface geometries.

articleTitle: Hilbert spectroscopy for security screening of liquids
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: To distinguish between liquids in security screening, we have applied Hilbert spectroscopy and high-T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> Josephson detectors. Compact set-ups have been developed and reflection spectra of various liquids in bottles have been measured in the spectral range of 15-300 GHz with scanning times down to 0.2 s.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization of photo-mixing generated signal using a single michelson interferometer
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We investigate the possibility to use a single interferometer, instead of two, to stabilize the frequency of a THz radiation generated by optical beating between two continuous-wave lasers.

articleTitle: Non-bias inspection of electrical failures in LSI interconnects using LTEM prototype system
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Logic LSI chips fabricated by 180nm process were measured by a prototype system of the laser terahertz emission microscope (LTEM). By comparing the LTEM images between a normal circuit and a defective one, p-n junction connected to the defective interconnect such as open or short circuits can be successfully determined under non-bias measurement condition. This result indicates that LTEM can be a useful tool which realizes a non-bias measurement of the defect localization in failure analysis of LSIs fabricated by 180nm process.

articleTitle: Differential-phase reflectometry using phased-array antenna system in QUEST
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The differential-phase reflectometry has been developed to measure the density profile, concerning electron Bernstein Wave (EBW) heating and current drive in the QUEST. The Phased Array Antenna (PAA) system was proposed for the reflectometry to improve the ratio of signal to noise. The PAA was confirmed to be effective, as a launching antenna to receive the larger reflected-wave signal.

articleTitle: In-orbit performace and calibration of SMILES
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Superconducting Submillimeter-Wave Limb-Emission Sounder (SMILES) is a sensor for atmospheric observation at 640 GHz from the International Space Station. Since the launch in Sep. 2009, SMILES has been showing the excellent observation performance. The results of SMILES development are summarized.

articleTitle: Room temperature Terahertz hot electron bolometric detector based on AlGaAs/GaAs two dimensional electron gas
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this paper, we present a hot-electron bolometric detector, which uses the nonlinearities of the heated two-dimensional electron gas medium in AlGaAs/GaAs at room temperature. The cooling process of the electrons is through the phonon-scattering mechanism. The response was measured at the 0.1-0.2 THz frequency range. The response was estimated, showing possible application of these detectors in sensing of Terahertz radiation.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic simulation of heterodyne terahertz detection in a field effect transistor
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We propose a method for the heterodyne detection of terahertz (THz) signals. The nonlinear element is constituted by the channel of an High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT), while the optical beating of two laser beams exciting plasma waves in the transistor channel plays the role of the THz local oscillator. We numerically show, through an hydrodynamic modelling, the efficiency of such a mixer.

articleTitle: Polarization dependent terahertz band pass filters with asymmetric cross shaped hole arrays
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Polarization dependent transmission of terahertz wave through the asymmetric cross shaped hole array was measured. Experimental results show good agreement with the simulated results. This filter can be used to such applications as THz spectroscopy and biological sensing.

articleTitle: Terahertz coherent scanning probe microscope
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present a terahertz (THz) scanning probe microscope which combines THz coherent spectrometer and scanning probe microscope. It detects forward-scattered radiation and employs harmonic signal demodulation to extract the signal of near-field contribution to scattering of THz electromagnetic waves.

articleTitle: Demonstration of high power terahertz sources driven by intense femtosecond lasers
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have demonstrated an intense plasma-based THz source using ∼5 TW femtosecond laser pulses to irradiate solid targets. The energy of a single THz pulse emitted in the laser specular direction increases with the laser energy. The maximum THz energy can be as high as tens µJ/sr. The polarization of the THz pulse is measured to be linear.

articleTitle: Propagation loss measurements of porous THz subwavelength fibers
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on the THz spectral loss characteristics of porous subwavelength polyethylene fibers. Propagation losses (α<;0.04cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>) were found to be comparable to non-porous fibers of equivalent diameter. However, the transmission peaks of porous fibers were broader and shifted to higher frequencies.

articleTitle: The role of multiphoton ionization by bicolor laser pulses in the description of THz pulse generation from laser breakdown plasma
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The ITM is used to describe the MI of atoms of gases under the bicolor femtosecond laser irradiation. The obtained formulas are applied for the qualitative explanation of recent experiments on the generation of THz radiation from an optical breakdown in a focus spot of a femtosecond laser in a gas.

articleTitle: High sensitive superconductor-semiconductor-superconductor THz detector
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We describe a high sensitivity THz detector based on the hot electron effect in a highly doped thin silicon semiconducting layer with tunnelling contacts to superconducting islands (S-Sm-S).

articleTitle: THz synthesizer for high resolution spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A THz synthesizer has been realized by phase locking the photomixer pump lasers to a frequency comb effectively locking the THz emission frequency of the source. This allowed the centre frequency of a molecular transition at 813 GHz to be measured with an accuracy of 20 kHz, (Δv/v ≈10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>).

articleTitle: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy on proteins, peptides, and small biological molecules
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Absorption coefficients and refractive indices of biologically important macromolecules such as lysozyme and myoglobin and small molecules such as adenosine triphosphate (ATP) have been obtained in the low-frequency region by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) to understand molecular dynamics and interactions of these molecules.

articleTitle: Investigating the role of water content on the terahertz properties of rat liver cirrhosis
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Existing studies terahertz pulsed imaging and spectroscopy to be safe techniques for biomedical applications. Coherent detection in terahertz pulsed imaging enable it to probe a wide range of information of unknown objects in both time and frequency domains. These distinctive features have recently spurred numerous research into human and animal tissues. We previously reported the dielectric properties of normal and diseased rat liver tissues by terahertz pulsed imaging. In this study, further experiments were carried out to understand the observed differences in the optical parameters by looking into the water contents of the normal and cirrhotic specimen.

articleTitle: Investigation of reflection-type cone condenser used for THz detectors
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A low cost and easy to fabricate THz triangle cone condenser with a high condensing efficiency in comparison to Winston cone has been made. A simulation and experimental results on condensing efficiency of both triangle cone and Winston cone show good consistency at the wavelength of 632.8 nm. In the case of Triangle cone condenser at the terahertz spectral region, simulation result showed that the condensing efficiency becomes approximately 100% at normal incident. In contrast to this, the condensing efficiency of Winston cone decreases at normal incident owing to the loss due to reflection. In general, the triangle cone has a broader field of view (FOV) than Winston cone, it is improved by attaching a baffle to the condenser.

articleTitle: Temperature and hydration-dependent THz investigations on proteins
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The far-infrared absorption of proteins is precisely measured at well-defined temperature and hydration. The absorption decreases with temperature and increases with hydration. The amount of water attached to the protein is calculated by a general sorption isotherm equation. Comparing this amount with the measured absorption the specific dynamic of the hydration shell can be extracted.

articleTitle: Time domain terahertz spectroscopy for investigating the dielectric relaxation dynamics of water in model membranes
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have investigated hydrated model membranes, formed by stacked bilayers of unsaturated lipids, by means of terahertz time-domain and infrared spectroscopy. Terahertz spectroscopy enables the investigation of water dynamics, owing to its sensitivity to dielectric relaxation processes associated with water reorientation. By controlling the number of water molecules per lipid molecule in the system, we elucidate how the interplay between the model membrane and water molecules results in different water dynamics. For decreasing hydration levels, we observe the appearance of new types of water dynamics: the collective bulklike dynamics become less pronounced, whereas an increased amount of both very slowly reorienting (i.e., irrotational) and very rapidly reorienting (i.e., fast) water molecules appear.

articleTitle: Terahertz spectroscopy of heavy and superheavy water vapors
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The paper reports on preliminary results of a study into a possibility of developing a fast method of atmospheric air analysis for the purpose of determination of the isotope composition of water vapors (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup>O, HD<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup>O, HTO) with the method of non-stationary terahertz (THz) range spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Simulation of the axis-encircling Cusp gun for Ka-band Gyro-TWT
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The Cusp electronic gun for Ka band Gyro-TWT is simulated by the 3D PIC software, in which the electronic 3D velocity value is extracted to calculate the velocity ratio of the transverse velocity and longitudinal velocity. The Cusp gun is designed and optimized in 98kV voltage and 1A current, to obtain 1.1 velocity ratio and 2.4% velocity spread. The design is adopt for the three folded helical corrugated waveguide Gyro-TWT.

articleTitle: A vector finite element Helmholtz solver
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The vector finite element method is used to solve the inhomogeneous Helmholtz equation to obtain the 3D circuit fields in resonant cavities. Numerical results will be shown for cylindrical and rectangular geometries to confirm the theoretical error estimates.

articleTitle: Utilization of collinear ECE detection/ECRH heating for active stabilization of plasma instabilities
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Experiments on TEXTOR have successfully demonstrated the proof of principle of using Electron Cyclotron Emission (ECE) measured along the Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ECRH) line-of-sight for the control of magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) modes. This work, which was done with a quasi-optical system, motivates the further development and implementation of a similar, but in-waveguide system for detection and control of Neoclassical Tearing Mode (NTM) in larger fusion machines. Progress on the implementation of such a system on ASDEX-Upgrade, based on waveguides equipped with a Fast Directional Switch (FADIS), is presented. Since FADIS, will be installed at ASDEX, to switch the gyrotron power between different launchers, FADIS can also be employed as a frequency filter serving the purpose of separating a low-power ECE signal from the high power ECRH radiation as required in the co-aligned ECE-ECRH setup. Because additional absorptive filtering is required after the FADIS ECE output in and a non resonant two-beam Mach-Zehnder-type interferometer was chosen. This system has been built and partially tested.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic pulse self-compression under cyclotron resonance absorption by plasma or electron beam
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Based on analogy to well known process of self-induced transparency of optical pulse propagating through passive two-level media we describe effect of electromagnetic pulse self-compression under conditions of cyclotron resonance absorption by plasma or electron beams.

articleTitle: The effect of optical delay line on THz differential time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The effect of optical delay line on THz differential time-domain spectroscopy (THz-DTDS) was studied, and we found that the optical delay line can significantly distort the THz DTDS signals due to sampling noise in lock-in detection.

articleTitle: Nonlinear generation and detection of THz pulses in ZnTe with chirped femtosecond laser pulses
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We show measurements and simulations of difference-frequency generation of THz pulses and subsequent free-space electro-optic sampling with prechirped femtosecond pulses in ZnTe. Negative prechirping enhances the efficiency due to compression of the laser pulse in the dispersive nonlinear crystal.

articleTitle: Multiple THz surface plasmon resonances of periodic split ring arrays in silicon
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: FDTD simulations of periodic split ring resonators in highly doped silicon show multiple THz surface plasmon resonances (SPR). The SPR frequency position may be tuned by modifying the split ring wall width, split angle and outer radius. These frequency tunable resonators are efficient THz detectors.

articleTitle: Multichannel THz imaging using arrays of photoconductive antennas
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In a new approach we report on a THz imaging system with arrays of horn-type photoconductive switches emitting in-plain. Aim is to combine the flexibility and sensitivity of THz antennas with the measurement speed of electro-optic sampling.

articleTitle: Improved performance of GaAs-based terahertz emitters
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have improved the stability and performance of terahertz photoconductive (Auston) switches using a combination of (NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S surface passivation and silicon nitride (Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) encapsulation. The passivation and encapsulation processes increased the average terahertz power generated four-fold.

articleTitle: Theoretical investigation of a high efficiency and broadband sub-terahertz gyrotron
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: This study investigates the electron dynamics of gyrotron interaction in a tapered waveguide and proposes an interaction structure for a 0.2-THz TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub> reflective gyrotron backward-wave oscillator (gyro-BWO). The design shows the advantages of high power, continuous and broadband frequency tuning, mode converter free, and inherently possesses mode-selective ability to suppress the potentially competing TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sub> mode. Calculated results indicate that the reflective TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub> gyro-BWO is capable of generating a peak power of 3.3 kW corresponding to 26.3% interacting efficiency with a broad 3dB-tuning-bandwidth of 6.9 GHz at beam current I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub> = 0.5 A and beam voltage V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub> = 25 kV.

articleTitle: Volumetric analyses using terahertz-tomography techniques
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report about an algorithmic approach to identify substances inside a sample using their complete characteristic absorption spectra from a tomographic measurement with ultrashort THz-pulses. Furthermore we show an algorithmic approach for tomographic reflection measurements.

articleTitle: Utilizing parallel plate waveguide modes for terahertz sensing
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Parallel-plate waveguide sensors are investigated by characterizing TM and TE modes when filled with inhomogeneous and homogeneous samples. Effects of multi-mode TE propagation within PPW and radiation patterns are investigated. Lactose detection is demonstrated by TDS and CW-VNA techniques.

articleTitle: Measurements of THz emission from nanometric-size transistors
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Measurements of terahertz resonant emission due to the excitation of plasma waves by an optical beating inside AlGaAs/InGaAs/InP high electron mobility transistors are reported at 300 K and 200 K.

articleTitle: THz quantum-cascade lasers with superconducting waveguides
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present THz quantum-cascade lasers in a superconducting double-metal waveguide. The active region is sandwiched between 300 nm thick Niobium layers. The current-voltage characteristic shows a pronounced photon kink at lasing threshold.

articleTitle: Dual wavelength cw microlaser for the generation of THz radiation
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Dual wavelength compact microlaser operation is demonstrated in the cw regime using a c-cut Nd doped GdVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> crystal. More than 200mW is obtained at these two wavelengths which are separated by 2.2nm leading to potential generation of 0.6THz radiation with this compact low-cost optical source.

articleTitle: Terahertz generation with tilted-front laser pulses: Dynamical theory predicts the ways to higher terahertz yield
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A dynamical theory of terahertz emission from a femtosecond laser pulse with tilted intensity front in an electro-optic crystal is developed. Applying the theory to GaAs pumped by a fiber laser and cryogenically cooled LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> pumped by a Ti:sapphire laser predicts the ways to higher terahertz yield.

articleTitle: Photo-electron gun generating sub-pico second bunch
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A 50 kV photo-electron gun was developed to construct a powerful broad-band terahertz radiation source. A magnesium photocathode was irradiated by a frequency tripled Ti:sapphire laser. Train of electron bunch of 50 pC was generated. The bunch produced the optical transition radiation at the beam dumper.

articleTitle: Theoretical model of a spark-gap for microwave generation
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Theoretical model of a sharpening spark-gap in an arbitrary electrical circuit is proposed. Simulation of operation of a spark-gap in the system including flux compression generator, transformer, explosive wires and microwave backward-wave tube is studied.

articleTitle: Bunch anomalies in SR-IR time domain emission
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A novel complex of time domain beam diagnostic tools integrated with SHT congruent calculus shows for the first time a direct evidence of a delayed component in the SR-IR emission of relativistic bunches of electrons and positrons at DAΦNE and HLS (Hefei Light Source). This evidence may lead to a paradox within the fundamental postulates of Special Relativity which implies a different value of light speed in vacuum. If it will not be considered valid, the paradox may be solved by discarding the “Rigid Bunch Model” in order to allow the bunch of relativistic particles to behave and evolve dynamically through a major collection of degrees of freedom, therefore exhibiting internal modes and/or “super-motions”.

articleTitle: Analysis of terahertz absorptions of structural isomers of tyrosine using a molecular orbital simulation and mid-infrared absorptions
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Differences in the terahertz spectral features and the assignment of terahertz absorptions and hydrogen bond networking of tyrosines were examined. The inter- and intra-molecular absorptions in a terahertz region were calculated by the structural optimization simulation “Gaussian 03” at B3LYP/6-31G (d) level using the mid-IR absorptions.

articleTitle: High-repetition-rate optical delay line using a micromirror array and galvanometer mirror
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have developed a high-speed optical delay line for the terahertz time-domain spectroscopy system (THz-TDS). The delay line is composed of a galvanometer mirror and a mirror array. We have demonstrated the acquisition of the time-domain wave form by using the delay line and a THz-TDS system.

articleTitle: A preliminary study towards the implementation of MIMO radar system for agriculture applications
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The revolution of MIMO radar system has the potential to be applied in many areas of applications such as in agriculture sector. It is inspired from MIMO system in telecommunications and uses multiple antennas to observe the different aspect of targets, hence produce high resolution radar image.

articleTitle: Differential Scanning Optical Microscopy with a THz quantum cascade laser source
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present a differential Near-field Scanning Optical Microscope (NSOM) operating with subwavelength resolution in the THz spectral region. The system, which employs a quantum cascade laser emitting at λ =105 μm as source, has been been tested on metal and graphite objects, with a resolution of ~ λ/10.

articleTitle: Hybrid continuous wave terahertz system
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present a hybrid continuous wave terahertz system, combining a two color photomixing system with a quasi time domain spectrometer, driven by a multimode laser diode. Overcoming the ambiguity of standard continuous wave thickness measurements is shown on different samples.

articleTitle: The reflectance and electrical properties of nanocrystalline metal Tm
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The reflectance spectra R(λ) within 200nm-2500nm wavelength range of the two nanocrystalline bulk metal thulium(Tm) samples were studied. The reflectivities R(λ) of Sample 1 and Sample 2 reach their minima 2.383% at 256nm and 3.439% at 214nm respectively. These minima correspond to the plasma oscillations in nanocrystalline bulk metal Tm.

articleTitle: Wedge-type negative index metamaterial at 0.5 THz
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Negative refraction through a fishnet related metamaterial is demonstrated at 0.5 THz. This characterization is based on refraction angle determination through a prism-like structure. The measurements are performed by means of a goniometric time-domain spectroscopy system while a numerical assessment is carried out by full wave electromagnetic analysis.

articleTitle: Coherent synchrotron terahertz radiation using electron bunch slicing
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Coherent and strong terahertz wave is generated from a synchrotron light source using laser bunch slicing. The electric field is detected with the electro-optic sampling method using a Ti:sapphire oscillator for probe and a 24-m long large mode-area photonic crystal fiber for delivering it.

articleTitle: The photoresponse of Hg0.722Cd0.278Te infrared photodiodes with a heavily doped n Region
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this paper, we report on two-dimensional (2D) numerical simulations of photoresponse for HgCdTe infrared photodiode. Effects of conduction band non-parabolic and band gap narrowing (BGN) have been investigated in detail. By taking into account the contributions: (i) the Burstein-Moss (BM) shift with a non-parabolic conduction band, (ii) the BGN effect, and (iii) the Hg-vacancy-induced acceptor trap level, we have obtained the photoresponse of Hg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.722</sub>Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.278</sub>Te infrared photodiode. Our simulation results are in good agreement with those in experiments.

articleTitle: Spectral sampling method for identification explosives
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Over the past few years rapid development of investigations in the THz area is observed. The research include spectral analysis of the THz signals to solve problem of materials identification as well. Results, published by various authors, concern one compound only, usually RDX but the problem of distinction of several compounds has received no attention yet. An examination of the identification systems is particularly important for the security systems to detect terrorist threat early enough. The THz range has been receiving particular attention recently for the reason of characteristic spectrum compounds peaks. Technological capabilities are not mature enough to analyze a wide THz range. It is however possible to develop narrow-band cascade lasers for this band. In this paper, a new concept of compounds identification, which bases on 14-subspectral definite (theoretical) THz detectors, is presented.

articleTitle: CCD-camera-based electro-optical detection of nanosecond THz pulses from an optical parametric oscillator
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report realization of a THz camera based on electro-optical detection of THz radiation from an optical parametric oscillator, using a silicon-based CCD camera as the optical detector. The dynamic range of 16.5 dB for a 6000-frame average (2-minute data acquisition time) is limited by laser noise.

articleTitle: Optimization of high-sensitive THz-wave detection using nonlinear up-conversion in DAST crystal
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A high-sensitivity, fast-response THz-wave detection using an organic nonlinear optical crystal of DAST has been demonstrated. In this report, the optimum performance of THz-wave detection was investigated in parameters such as the thickness of DAST, pump wavelength, and pumping intensity. Consequently, a higher sensitivity was obtained.

articleTitle: A terahertz light emitter of a semiconductor-multilayer coupled cavity by frequency-mixing-signal generation
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A coupled-cavity structure for terahertz light emitting devices is proposed. Strong frequency-mixing signal of the two cavity modes of the multilayer coupled-cavity on a (113)B GaAs substrate was observed. We found that an asymmetric structure was essential to emit a difference frequency light by a simulation of the optical field in the cavity.

articleTitle: Parametric study on the effect of the dielectric and geometry properties on the parasitics in gyrotron beam tunnels
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Using the numerical code Fishbone, developed to study the parasitic oscillations in gyrotron beam tunnels, a parametric study is performed on the effect of the dielectric material as well as of the slot geometry on the growth rate of the excited parasitic modes.

articleTitle: Sub-Terahertz spectroscopy in superconductors and charge-ordered materials
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We review the results obtained on novel superconductors and on materials showing Charge Density Waves (CDW), which have in common the application of the Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer theory, by using Coherent synchrotron Radiation as a source for sub-Terahertz spectroscopy. We also present new data on the low-energy excitations of the CDW pahse of multiferroic LuFe(2)O(4).

articleTitle: Frequency-dependent response of two-contact photoconductive antenna
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A two-contact photoconductive antenna has been experimentally found to be frequency-dependent and respond to the mixture of both polarization components of terahertz radiation. This effect leads to wrong polarization state measurement results. It may also result in a fake “absorption peak”.

articleTitle: Field effect transistors for fast terahertz detection and imaging
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Recent results on THz detection by FETs are reported. THz Imaging with FET and detection in quantizing magnetic field. Results of THz Imaging show that FETs arrays are good candidate for real time imaging. In magnetic field we report an enhancement of signal at the cyclotron resonance condition.

articleTitle: Quantitative measurement captan and riadimefon residue by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy was used to measure terahertz far-infrared spectral characteristics of two pesticides (captan, riadimefon) at room temperature. From the experimental results, a series of characteristic absorption peaks can be observed between 0.2 THz and 3.0 THz. Comprehensive analysis of two pesticides absorption spectrum and refractive index of spectral features, we can find that their absorption and refractive index spectrum are very different. We have studied THz spectra of molecular forms of nitrofen based on the density functional theory (DFT). These feature absorption spectra are helpful to form a basis for pesticide spectral library.

articleTitle: Analysis of optical THz-signals from mode-locked semiconductor laser by using a semiconductor optical amplifier-based detection scheme
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: An all-optical approach based on nonlinear interactions inside a semiconductor optical amplifier for measuring the THz beat-tone of a passively mode-locked laser is proposed. This novel approach can be applied to beat-tones in the range from GHz to few THz.

articleTitle: New 2D TeraHertz sensor based on arrayed thermal converter coupled to infrared temperature flux measurement
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We defined the Terahertz Thermal Converters concept to design a device for 2D THz imaging. Coupled to an infrared temperature flux sensors, we demonstrate an absolute auto-calibrated Terahertz power-meter (>10μW) enable to characterized THz spatial beam profile of CW sources.

articleTitle: Broadband transmission of terahertz radiations in thin silica tube
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Hollow-core thin silica tubes based on antiresonant guiding mechanism are studied with Terahertz (THz) time domain spectroscopy (TDS) setup. By controlling the parameters of the waveguide, broad transmission windows, up to 580 GHz, is demonstrated at terahertz frequencies.

articleTitle: Spin related effect in Terahertz photovoltaic response of Si-MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on investigations of photovoltaic response of Si-MOSFETs subjected to Terahertz radiation in high magnetic fields. The MOSFETs develop a dc drain-to-source voltage that shows singularities in magnetic fields corresponding to paramagnetic resonance conditions. These singularities are investigated as a function of incident frequency, temperature and two-dimensional carrier density. We tentatively attribute these resonances to spin transitions of the electrons bounded to Si dopants and discuss the possible physical mechanism of the photovoltaic signal generation.

articleTitle: Consideration of refraction losses for time-domain terahertz computed tomography
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Terahertz computed tomography has been performed using a time-domain terahertz spectrometer. Refraction losses induced by the transmission of the terahertz radiation through the samples have been taken into account in order to reconstruct the three-dimensional aspect of complex shape objects.

articleTitle: Antenna measurement system operating at W and J millimeter wave bands
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A millimeter wave antenna measurement system is presented. The frequencies of operation are around 100 GHz and 300 GHz (W/J Bands). The facility is a single reflector compact range system. Design tasks deal with the serrated reflector and the corresponding millimeter wave instrumentation design.

articleTitle: The design of a 390 GHz gyrotron based on a cusp electron gun
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A 390 GHz harmonic gyrotron based on a cusp electron gun was designed to operate on a TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">71</sub> mode and the 7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> cyclotron harmonic of a large orbit electron beam. This beam is produced by a cusp electron gun with a voltage of 40 keV, a current of 1.5 A and an adjustable velocity ratio from 1 to 3. Smooth cylindrical waveguide was studied and built as the interaction cavity. The relationship between the cavity dimensions and cavity Q was optimized for output at the design mode. A simple linear output taper with moderate mode conversion was used in the gyrotron output. Both theoretical analysis and numerical simulation results (using the 3D PIC code MAGIC) of this gyrotron will be presented. When the beam thickness and beam spread were introduced into the simulation, competitive modes were observed in the simulation resulting in a drop in the output power. A high frequency (325-500 GHz) VNA was used to measure the millimeter wave properties of the gyrotron cavity and the results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Terahertz emission from InAs and InSb under a 1.55 µm Laser Excitation
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Terahertz (THz) emission from a 1.55 μm laser excitation on InAs and InSb was investigated. InAs showed a much higher emission as compared to InSb that differs from earlier reports. Semiconductor quality or different surface conditions could be the cause of this unexpected result.

articleTitle: Specific features of terahertz radiation from air plasma generated by both the first and the second optical harmonics
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The theory describing specific features of the source of terahertz waves generated due to the breakdown of air by both the first and the second harmonics of laser pulse is introduced. The approach considers inside physics of low frequency current formation during the ionization.

articleTitle: Solvation water of biomolecules seen through THz glasses
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The THz absorption of the intermolecular vibrational modes of the hydrogen bond network of water has recently been found to define a dynamical solvation shell around solutes that extends beyond the first hydration layer. Here, we study the vibrations and dynamical processes in the hydrogen bond network of water using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to understand its properties.

articleTitle: Status of the ITER electron cyclotron H&CD system
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: This paper presents the status of the design and the integration of the 20 MW EC H&CD system under development for the ITER Tokamak. Progress includes agreement on the first set of procurement arrangements (EC Transmission Line and the RF building housing both IC and EC systems), advancing the design of all components to either the conceptual or preliminary design stage, optimization of gyrotrons performances and finalization of launchers design.

articleTitle: High temperature performance of a diagonal THz-QCL calculated with non-equilibrium Green's function method
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have calculated the performance of a novel diagonal design-based THz-QCLs with the non-equilibrium Green's function method. The diagonal QCL has a THz gain even at 200 K. The main origin for this is that the non-radiative losses are better suppressed than the optical transition.

articleTitle: Dynamical Franz-Keldysh effect in GaAs induced by monocycle terahertz pulse
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We studied electron-hole behaviors interacted with intense THz pulse in GaAs MQW. THz pulse causes strong modulations of exciton in absorption spectrum. For high THz electric fields, hh exciton energy shows blueshift proportional to THz electric field squared, due to dynamical Franz-Keldysh effect.

articleTitle: Resonance frequency shifts of rectangular holes on finite dielectric substrates
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We observe that rectangular holes fabricated in a gold film with a sub-skindepth thickness show blue-shifted resonance frequencies as the width increases. For rectangular holes on a finite substrate its thickness and the hole width are crucial factors determining the resonance frequency.

articleTitle: Development of mechanically detected ESR in terahertz region
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have developed a high-frequency ESR technique using a cantilever. In this method, magnetization change caused by ESR absorption is detected as cantilever deflection. In this study, spin sensitivity as high as 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> spins/Gauss was achieved at 80 GHz by an optical modulation method. We also succeeded in angle-dependent ESR measurement at 80 GHz using a cantilever.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a terahertz detector based on a superconducting tunnel junction coupled to a thin superconductor film
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The principle of a superconducting terahertz detector is verified. We have detected terahertz radiation based on the Cooper-pair breaking process, and confirmed that the sensitivity has a sharp increase around 0.7 THz, a value that is in agreement with the gap frequency of the superconducting Nb.

articleTitle: Terahertz form birefringent devices
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present photonic crystals exhibiting a pronounced form birefringence at terahertz frequencies. These crystals can be employed as volumetric birefringent elements for a broad frequency range. Along with a theoretical discussion we demonstrate measurement results of a polymeric crystal.

articleTitle: Optical parametric oscillator for continuous wave terahertz generation by optical heterodyning
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: New continuous-wave singly resonant optical parametric oscillator (OPO) based on a bulk Bragg grating is presented. The OPO produces two coherent and spatially overlapping near-infrared beams with their frequency difference in the terahertz regime.

articleTitle: Layer-by-layer photoluminescence and photoreflectance analysis of impurity distribution in HgCdTe
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Layer-by-layer infrared photoluminescence and photoreflectance measurements are performed on an HgCdTe epliayer. The Cd composition and impurity states along the growth direction are examined, and the vertical distribution is discussed.

articleTitle: THz power measurement traceable to the International System of Units
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: THz power measurements traceable to the International System of Units were missing in the past. Investigations of two optical methods source- and detector-based radiometry led to the design of a new calibration facility for THz detectors by a molecular gas laser and a room-temperature radiometer.

articleTitle: 2 MW CW RF load for Gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Gyrotrons are in development to produce 2 MW CW of RF power in the mm-wave frequency range. Developers require RF loads to test these devices at full power, and similar loads will be required for ITER. This presentation describes development of a 2 MW CW RF load to meet these requirements.

articleTitle: Numerical study of pseudospark discharge based electron beam and propagation for terahertz source generation
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The Terahertz band of EM spectrum has received considerable research interests recently. A micro-klystron has the potential to meet the requirement of high power and compact terahertz source in many applications. The micro-klystron needs a very thin electron beam with sufficient current density. A pseudospark discharge cathode has the ability to provide high current density with small diameter electron beam (<;1mm).

articleTitle: Investigations of room temperature bolometers for THz applications
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We investigate in this work the performance of two configurations of room temperature bolometers dedicated to THz applications. Fabrication processes, noise level, sensitivity and resolution characterizations are presented. Results emphasize the efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Development of a compact sub-terahertz second-harmonic gyrotron
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A versatile and compact sub-THz second harmonic gyrotron with output parameters suitable for various spectroscopic studies is under development now at FIR FU Research Center. Here we present and discuss the results of the initial computer-aided design (CAD) of this novel prospective member of the Gyrotron FU CW series.

articleTitle: Micro-fabricated millimeter wave vacuum electronic devices
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: 0.1 THz Coupled Cavity Backward-wave Oscillator (CCBWO) is being developed utilizing two-step X-ray lithography. The characteristics of this 0.1 THz CCBWO are investigated through cold and hot tests.

articleTitle: Amplification of picosecond pulses in a 140 GHz gyro-TWT
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report amplification of pulses as short as 400 ps in a 1 kW, 140 GHz gyro-TWT amplifier. To our knowledge, this is the first observation of picosecond pulse amplification in a gyro-amplifier. The pulses show measurable broadening due to two distinct phenomena: group velocity dispersion and spectral narrowing due to the finite gain bandwidth. Theoretical analysis is in good agreement with the observed broadening of the pulses. Picosecond pulses are useful for applications in spectroscopy and advanced radar.

articleTitle: Simulation of electrical and optical characteristics for InP/InGaAs/InP p-i-n photodiodes
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: 2D simulation of dark current and photoresponse for InP/InGaAs/InP photodiode is carried out by Sentaurus DEVICE. The simulation results are in good agreement with experiments confirming that generation-recombination effect is the dominant source of dark current at low bias.

articleTitle: Comparative study of extraction of material parameters from THz time-domain spectroscopy performed in reflection and in transmission
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We model and compare the uncertainties of the refractive index and the coefficient of absorption of materials in the far-infrared, determined from THz time-domain spectroscopy performed in reflection and in transmission. Our study is experimentally validated. We give rules to select the most appropriate experimental technique regarding studied samples.

articleTitle: Design of low loss single-mode terahertz Bragg fibers based on a confinement loss diagram
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this paper, the confinement loss diagram (CLD) is combined with the modal filtering approach to design low loss single-mode terahertz (THz) Bragg fibers. To filter out the TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode, the confinement loss diagram is exploited to locate a cutoff point which allows the use of a larger air core. Consequently, a lower loss can be obtained while only the HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> can propagate effectively. The designed Bragg fiber can achieve simulated propagation loss around 0.2 dB/m to 0.5 dB/m in the range of 0.7 THz to 1.4 THz, with only 10 layers of Bragg cladding.

articleTitle: Design and simulations of a micromachined Golay-cell based THz sensors for room temperature imaging applications
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A novel broadband THz microsensor for room temperature imaging applications is presented. The sensor's response time is optimized by tuning its structural design, using Monte-Carlo and transient FEM simulations. The optimized and robust sensor shows a 3.5 THz bandwidth (0.5-4 THz) and a response time of ~40 ms, suitable for real time radio visualization.

articleTitle: Elaboration of 260 GHz second harmonic CW gyrotron with high stability of output parameters for DNP spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Results of elaboration of continuous-wave 258.6 GHz gyrotron with output power about 100 W with high stability of output parameters is presented. This paper includes results of calculation, design, experiments and technical requirements for main subsystems of gyrotron and auxiliaries. The gyrotron setup is a main part of a complex experimental system for NDP spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Thickness dependence of intense terahertz emission from InAs thin films
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A systematic study of the intense terahertz (THz) emission from InAs thin films grown on a GaAs substrate was performed by varying the V/III ratio of the InAs. The emission intensity increased as the film thickness increased up to 1 μm and became stronger than that from a p-type InAs substrate for sample of lower V/III ratio. The mechanism of the enhanced THz emission is discussed, and a possible mechanism for the thickness dependence is also presented.

articleTitle: Gyrotron interaction simulations with tapered magnetostatic field
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We investigate the interaction of the electron beam with the RF wave in a gyrotron, in the presence of an axially tapered magnetic field. The simulation results of three interaction codes are compared and the different modellings are discussed.

articleTitle: THz-TDS of filter paper at differing humidities
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Characterisation of filter paper using Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy (THz-TDS) is given at different humidities. This is achieved using saturated salt solutions. The absorption coefficient of filter paper increases with frequency and relative humidity.

articleTitle: Performance of a compact, continuous-wave terahertz source based on a quantum-cascade laser
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on the development of a compact, easy-to-use terahertz radiation source, which combines a quantum-cascade laser (QCL) with a compact, low-input-power Stirling cooler. The QCL, which is based on a two-miniband design, has been developed for high output and low electrical pump power. Special care has been taken to achieve a good thermal coupling between the QCL and the cold finger of the cooler. The whole system weighs less than 15 kg including the cooler and power supplies. The maximum output power is 8 mW at 3.1 THz. With an appropriate optical beam shaping, the emission profile of the laser is fundamental Gaussian. The applicability of the system is demonstrated by imaging and molecular-spectroscopy experiments.

articleTitle: FEM with high-selective Bragg resonator based on coupling of propagating and cutoff waves
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Bragg FEM with a two-mirror resonator including advanced Bragg structure based on coupling of propagating and quasi-cutoff waves was studied. Implication of the cutoff wave into the feedback loop improves selectivity of the Bragg resonators over transverse coordinates and allows advance of FEM into short wavelengths up to THz-band. Operability of Bragg resonator of a novel type has been demonstrated in Ka-band JINR-IAP FEM.

articleTitle: Heating of Si wafer using a sub-THz gyrotron FU CW V as a radiation source
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Heating effect of sub-THz radiation on Si Wafer is studied by using a Gyrotron FU CW V as a sub-THz radiation source. Increasing rate of the temperature is measured for several frequencies ranged from 75 GHz to around 200 GHz. The highest increasing rate reaches 39 degree/sec at the frequency of 203 GHz at 100W. The skin effect of sub-THz radiation is considered to analyze the measurement results.

articleTitle: Neural Network-based non-destructive quantification of thin coating by terahertz pulsed imaging in the frequency domain
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Terahertz pulsed imaging (TPI) is a powerful tool for non-destructive quantification of pharmaceutical tablet coatings. In this paper, we present a Neural Network (NN) based method for extracting the coating thickness from the FFT-amplitude of the measured terahertz waveform. We demonstrate that the NN-based frequency domain method outperforms the standard “peak-finding” time-domain method, in terms of quantifying thinner coating thickness, although a learning set of data is necessary.

articleTitle: Emission of terahertz radiation from two-dimensional electron systems in semiconductor nano-heterostructures
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: This paper reviews recent advances in terahertz (THz) emission from two-dimensional (2D) electron systems in semiconductor nano-heterostructures. The topics cover i) broadband THz emission from 2D plasmons in III-V heterojunction transistors and ii) amplified stimulated THz emission from fs-laser pumped graphene heterostructures.

articleTitle: Terahertz detection and emission by field effect transistors: Influence of high magnetic fields and channel geometry
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We review a few recent results concerning the physics and applications of FETs as Terahertz detectors and emitters. Particularly we stress results concerning dependance of THz detection and emission on high/quantizing magnetic fields and the geometry of the FETs channel.

articleTitle: High resolution measurements to determine the permittivity in artificial structures
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The characterization of materials is one major task for systems which work e.g. in the field of quality or production control. One factor to analyze material volume information is the permittivity. The following paper describes a measurement method to determine and gives an overview about the measurement system. In addition first measurement results will be shown.

articleTitle: Validation of the AVTIS volcano imager radiometry — A comparison of infrared and millimetre wave thermal imagery
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The AVTIS remote sensing instrument is a custom built millimetre wave sensor that has been developed as a practical field tool for remote sensing of volcanic terrain at active lava domes. We present validation of the MMW radiometry of a volcanic scene by comparison with coincident infrared imagery.

articleTitle: Nondestructive detection of delaminations in plastic weld joints
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Nondestructive evaluation has an increased industrial interest especially in the plastic industry. One of the challenging tasks is the detection of delaminations in plastic weld joints. We present a technique to find a delamination employing contact-free, nondestructive terahertz time-domain spectroscopy and a smart algorithm employing a cascaded fourier transform.

articleTitle: Electrodynamics of confined water in nanospace
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: By the measurements of microwave conductivity, terahertz transmission and infrared spectroscopy, we clarify that the two-dimensionally confined water forms hexamer cluster in the MnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> interlayer of Na-birnessite, and the hydration states around PO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> depend on the type of metallic ions of M-DNA.

articleTitle: To the theory of high-power gyrotrons with uptapered resonators
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The effect of a slight uptapering of the resonator wall on the efficiency enhancement and the purity of the radiation spectrum in the process of the gyrotron start-up and power modulation are studied for a typical high-power 170 GHz gyrotron which is currently under development in Europe for ITER.

articleTitle: Dielectric behavior of water in THz influenced by alkali and alkaline-earth halides
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A transmission type THz-TDS was applied to study dielectric behavior of water including NaCl and MgCl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Imaginary part of the complex dielectric constant below 1THz and the dielectric slow relaxation time were evaluated and disclosed that they are dependent on the type of salt and the concentration.

articleTitle: Effect of electric field distribution in the magnetron-injection gun region on electron beam characteristics in gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A method for control of electric field distribution in the near-cathode region of a magnetron-injection gun has been developed. The possibility to improve quality of the helical electron beam by regulated non-uniformities of electric field is studied experimentally and using computer modeling.

articleTitle: Study for high transmission efficiency in long distance transmission line
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The transmission mode purity in ITER relevant long distance transmission line was measured. Although the transmission power included 95% HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> at the input of the transmission line, HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> power was reduced as 91% after transmission through 40 m long transmission line with 6 miter bends and a waveguide switch. This was caused by mode conversion loss in transmission components.

articleTitle: Measurement of the complex dielectric constant of volcanic ash at millimetre wavelengths
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Methods for determining the dielectric permittivity of rock samples at millimetre wave frequencies have been investigated. A quasi-optical approach using pellets of powdered samples was found to work well, avoiding the dimensional restrictions of small waveguides. The permittivity of volcanic rock and ash samples was measured, providing valuable data for MMW radar remote sensing of terrain and ash clouds.

articleTitle: Microwave Cherenkov radiation from a particle-in-flight to a semi-infinite layered medium
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Some part of the microwave Cherenkov radiation from a particle-in-flight from vacuum to semi-infinite layered medium is redirected by the periodical structure of medium in the backward direction. This part of radiation proves to be quasi-monochromatic.

articleTitle: A thin-film spiral antenna coupled with Bi microbolometer operating at 100 GHz band
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A thin-film 2-arm spiral antenna with Bi microbolometer operating at 100 GHz band was fabricated. In the video detection, detected voltages, which were proportional to the power of signal wave at 94 GHz and a bias current, were obtained. DC sensitivity of the microbolometer was about 35 W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>.

articleTitle: Experimental and theoretical study of photoconductive short electrical pulses generation at high repetition rate
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have studied the generation of ps electrical pulses at high repetition rate using photoconductive antenna. Experimentation and simulation show that screening of the biasing electrical field occurs much after the trapping time scale of the free carriers leading to a strong decrease of the signal.

articleTitle: Time-domain coherent Raman spectroscopy in THz frequency region
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Time-domain coherent-Raman spectroscopy in the THz frequency region using a mode-locked femtosecond laser was studied. In this report, we attempted to detect the coherent Raman signal with an improved SNR owing to the averaging effect of the high-repetition frequency femtosecond laser.

articleTitle: A new single shot terahertz time domain spectrometer for rapid product and process control
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A new simple time-domain THz spectrometer based on a single-shot balanced detection of the electric field is presented. It allows for the recording of the full temporal THz profile at kHz acquisition rates. Its performances are demonstrated by measuring the fast drying process of acetone on Teflon.

articleTitle: Optical characterization of a superconducting hotspot air-bridge bolometer
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A superconducting bolometer with an on-chip lithographic terahertz antenna has been characterized in passive and active mode. Direct detection measurements made with 300K/77K blackbody sources yeld an optical efficiency of 10%. Time response of the bolometer has been obtained at 2.5 and 4.4 THz by illuminating the detector with quantum cascade lasers (QCL) showing a time constant of 1.2 μs. Here we report on the fabrication and the optical characterization of an antenna-coupled hot-spot microbolometer operating in vacuum at liquid helium temperature.

articleTitle: Substrateless micrometric metal mesh for mid-infrared plasmonic sensors
publicationTitle: 35th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We fabricated large-area substrateless metal meshes with micrometric period. The measured mid-infrared (IR) spectra display resonant features with high Q-factor due to the interaction of the radiation with Surface Plasmon (SP) modes on both faces of the film. The devices can be used for SP-based sensors.

articleTitle: An innovative non invasive technique for treatment of works of art. MM and THz waves for diagnostics and conservation
